rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track

SELECT ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assumption: "most albums" means counting rows in the Album table per artist, and I'll return all artists tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC
SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS full_name, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS total_spent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: total spent is the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming "looks after" means Customer.SupportRepId, and ties would all be returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId)
rows.note: Assumption: "never been purchased" means the track does not appear in any InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2012, grouped by BillingCountry.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3 ORDER BY ar.Name
rows.note: Assuming "tracks" link to artists via Track → Album → Artist, and genres via Track.GenreId.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC
rows.note: I'll compute revenue per genre from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity), then divide by the overall total.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM Invoice i2
    JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  )

SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2011-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2012-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total by invoice date month in 2011.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_purchase FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_purchase >= '2010-01-01' AND first_purchase < '2011-01-01'
SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS minutes FROM Album a JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql: WITH yearly AS (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS year, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY year) SELECT year, revenue, ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year), 1) AS yoy_pct_change FROM yearly ORDER BY year
WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average FROM cust WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM cust)

WITH pa AS (
  SELECT pt.PlaylistId, al.ArtistId
  FROM PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
),
counts AS (
  SELECT PlaylistId, COUNT(DISTINCT ArtistId) AS n FROM pa GROUP BY PlaylistId
)
SELECT p.Name, c.n AS distinct_artists
FROM counts c
JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = c.PlaylistId
WHERE c.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM counts)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1)

SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRep, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue2010
FROM Invoice i
JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
ORDER BY Revenue2010 DESC
LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'll treat "invoice revenue" as the sum of `Invoice.Total` for 2010 invoices, grouped by each customer's support rep.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1'
rows.note: Discontinued is stored as TEXT '0' or '1', so I'll count rows where Discontinued = '1'.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany'
SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming "most products" means the count of rows in Products per category, with ties all shown.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assuming each order's Freight is averaged per shipper via Orders.ShipVia joined to Shippers.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e JOIN Employees m ON e.ReportsTo = m.EmployeeID WHERE m.FirstName = 'Andrew' AND m.LastName = 'Fuller'

SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY EmployeeID))
rows.note: Assumption: "handled" means the employee recorded on the order (Orders.EmployeeID), counting orders with OrderDate in 2020, and ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products)
rows.note: Assumption: "average product unit price" is the mean of Products.UnitPrice across all products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_to_france FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France'
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped to France" means Orders.ShipCountry = 'France' (orders with a non-null ShippedDate are not required; I'll count all orders destined for France).

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5

SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName

WITH r AS (
  SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2021-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2022-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.CustomerID
)
SELECT CompanyName, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM r
WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM r)
rows.note: I'll sum revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over 2021 orders, grouped by customer, and return the top one (ties included).

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming "most orders" means the count of rows in Orders by OrderDate month for the year 2021.

rows.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Orders o JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '1997' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID) SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, n AS OrderCount FROM t WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM t)
rows.note: No employee handled any orders in 1997. The Orders table only covers 2012 to 2023, so there is no 1997 data to rank.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and days are computed as the difference between julianday(ShippedDate) and julianday(OrderDate).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Orders o2 JOIN Customers c2 ON c2.CustomerID = o2.CustomerID WHERE o2.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o2.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c2.Country))

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023'
rows.note: Assuming "2023 sales" means orders with OrderDate in 2023, and revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_every_month_2020 FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12)

WITH ov AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID, o.OrderID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS v
  FROM Orders o JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID
),
ea AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, AVG(ov.v) AS avg_value
  FROM ov JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ov.EmployeeID
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID
)
SELECT full_name, ROUND(avg_value, 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM ea
WHERE avg_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_value) FROM ea)

WITH rev AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID
)
SELECT CompanyName, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM rev
WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev)
rows.note: I'll assume revenue is `UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)` from Order Details, with 2018 determined by `OrderDate`, and return all suppliers tied for the top total.
